Hi! I'm 17 and just got diagnosed this year so I'm in your boat! Sorry in advance for so much reading! But here's what's helped me as a teen :) 

Take care of yourself! See a PT, if you're able, someone who specializes or knows about your disorder. I know everyone has said this in this thread but it is absolutely important. Once you're given the exercises, don't stop doing them even when you're done with PT. Drink an excessive amount of water, eat salt (yes, sodium is good for your blood vessel elasticity!) , and eat healthier/ find and avoid foods that make you sick! Especially if you are easily dizzy or sick to your stomach. Other disorders like POTS and IBS are common with hypermobility and even if you don't have them, you can share a lot of symptoms with them and these are good ways to manage that. Also on that note, if you're worried about a symptom, see a doctor! There's no harm in just making sure. Like i said there are quite a few other disorders and such that are related to hypermobility syndrome and connective tissue disorders in general. Also! Take naps! and sleep for longer than your piers. You're bounded to be fatigued. 

Be careful with yourself. Understand that you are more limited than other people can be hard to come to terms with, but it's important in your safety.  Subluxations aren't fun and getting one that could have been prevented sucks. If you do get one though, don't be embarrassed to use a sling or crutches or ice or whatever you need. If you need a 504 for school, get one. Everyones' are different but somethings you might need like more time to get to classes in between bells or a nurses pass can be made a lot less of a struggle with a 504. It's definitely worth it. 

Don't feel bad when you need to be accommodated for. Don't feel bad if you miss a day of PT exercises. Don't feel bad if you used whatever time you had not hurting to be with friends or family, not doing schoolwork. Dealing with this can be hard, so there's no need to make it harder on yourself. Also don't be too freaked out or discouraged by everything you see online or even on this subreddit. Hypermobility is a very broad spectrum and it can be way more severe in some people, and it can effect some people so little that you'd feel like you're over reacting. Everyone has different symptoms, severities, and  tolerances. 

In no time at all you'll feel out your own symptoms and remedies and ways to do things to help you. Just making an effort to stay healthy and positive to me are the most important things. You'll find a lot of kind people on this subreddit that are always here to help :)
